reviewed_by: Automated source-semantic review by the delegated coding agent against live Binary Ninja 6.0.10601 (MCP), Radare2 6.2.0, angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast and an ad-hoc retail-ESIL/host-built differential
review_basis: The working-tree revision of engine/src/retail/core/app_startup_natives.cpp read for this report hashes to 337c5d5726e7d7ddc366dcece75a990ccdf7b7d436a8cf15a930b12e911dba3a and its header hashes to 790a989331d01be1a96fe9e7136374f2f524d6f5f216a9f3e1a534c0ad026b50. The retail body was disassembled and decompiled through the live Binary Ninja MCP view, recovered independently with Radare2 6.2.0 and angr CFGFast at the exact entry, and the candidate function was exercised against the retail bytes in Radare2 ESIL for ten 32-bit values. This review also re-checked the global identity: retail 0x0048F0B0 reads 0x005C8BD4, which 0x0048F100 writes and 0x0048F090 (the instance-handle getter) does not touch.

binary_ninja.result: range 0x0048F0B0-0x0048F0B6 (6 bytes), 1 basic block, 0 incoming/outgoing edges inside the function, 0 callees; prototype int32_t() with the default cdecl convention; disassembly mov eax,dword [0x5c8bd4]; retn; HLIL return g_5c8bd4; memory read a1d48b5c00c390909090909090909090; single caller callsite 0x4988DD in function 0x4988D0.

radare2.result: function size 6, nbbs 1, ninstrs 2, edges 0, calltype cdecl, nargs 0, indegree 1, outdegree 0; bytes a1d48b5c00c3; axt reports the only call site 0x4988dd (caller fcn.004988d0), the data read at 0x48f0b0 and the only data write to 0x005c8bd4 at 0x48f10c.

angr.result: exact entry 0x0048F0B0 recovered; function_entry 0x0048F0B0, block_count 1, nodes ['0x0048F0B0'], edges [], returning true, has_unresolved_jumps false, result pass; binary SHA-256 dea34892... loaded at mapped base 0x400000 with bits 32.

global_identity.writer: 0x0048F100 (Binary Ninja: BOOL FX_ExplosionSpawn_23(BOOL arg1)) loads HWND from 0x005C8BC4, loads the argument from [esp+4], tests the HWND, stores the argument to 0x005C8BD4 at 0x0048F10C, and if the HWND is non-zero calls SetWindowTextA(hwnd, argument) through IAT 0x005331DC. Binary Ninja pseudocode: g_5c8bd4 = arg1; if (!hwnd) return arg1; return SetWindowTextA(hwnd, arg1).
global_identity.main_call: Retail main 0x0048F530 pushes the literal 0x0053B534 ("Innerloop") at 0x0048F609 and calls 0x0048F100 at 0x0048F60E, so the start-up value of 0x005C8BD4 is the window-title string pointer.
global_identity.reader: The only reader of 0x005C8BD4 is this getter. Its caller 0x4988D0 (0x4988DD) uses the return value as MessageBoxA's lpCaption: Binary Ninja pseudocode calls MessageBoxA(AppContext_GethWnd(), arg1, FX_FireBallUpdate_22(), MB_ICONHAND).
global_identity.not_the_instance_handle: The instance handle is written to 0x005C8BC0 by 0x0048F0D0 and read by the separate getter 0x0048F090, whose bytes are a1 c0 8b 5c 00 c3 (mov eax,[0x005C8BC0]; ret). 0x0048F0B0's moffs operand is d4 8b 5c 00 (0x005C8BD4), so the earlier candidate body returning the InstanceHandle global was a wrong-global transcription.
global_identity.search_scope: axt @ 0x5c8bd4 in a fully analysed Radare2 session and Binary Ninja data cross-references agree on exactly one writer (0x0048F10C) and one reader (0x0048F0B0); a byte search for 0x0048F0B0 as image data found no function-pointer table entry.

host_differential.tool: Radare2 6.2.0 ESIL (retail bytes) versus a host-built translation unit (candidate), ad-hoc script at /tmp/taskb_getters.py
host_differential.result: Ten 32-bit values (0, 1, 0x1000, 0x400000, 0x5C8BD4, 0x7FFFFFFF, 0x80000000, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xDEADBEEF, 0xFFFFFFFF) were seeded at retail 0x005C8BD4, the retail getter was executed from 0x0048F0B0, and the candidate GetAppTitle was called with AppTitle seeded to the same bits while CommandLine and InstanceHandle held distinct sentinels. All ten returned the seeded value, left AppTitle unchanged, and left InstanceHandle unchanged; 10/10 matched.
host_differential.durability: This is a one-off command, not a committed runner case in scripts/native_diff_runner.py; no committed runner case exists for this address.

observed_semantics.return_value: EAX receives the 32-bit dword loaded from 0x005C8BD4 on the only path

candidate_semantics.function: char const* IGI_RETAIL_CDECL GetAppTitle() { return AppTitle; }
candidate_semantics.behavior: No arguments. One 4-byte load of the separate AppTitle global into EAX followed by a return. No branch, call, arithmetic, floating-point operation or write.

global.written_by: nothing in the current engine build; retail 0x0048F100 (SetAppTitle) has only an unlinked GameNatives transcription at scripts/GameNatives/fx/0048F100-SetAppTitle.cpp
global.separation: AppTitle is a distinct 4-byte global (.bss+0 in the fresh object); InstanceHandle is .bss+4 and CommandLine .bss+8, so the getter can no longer return the instance handle. Those offsets belong to the recorded -O3 object and would change if the translation unit were relinked with other code.

object.function_sha_shape: GetAppTitle is 6 bytes: a1 <dir32 .bss+0>; c3, the same 6-byte load/return shape as retail

checks.name: function_identity
checks.rationale: Binary Ninja, Radare2 6.2.0 and angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast each recover exactly one function at 0x0048F0B0 spanning 6 bytes with 2 instructions, one basic block and no edges. The current translation unit defines exactly one function for this address, GetAppTitle returning the AppTitle global.

checks.name: argument_mapping
checks.rationale: The retail body reads no argument slot and Binary Ninja gives it the cdecl no-argument prototype int32_t(); Radare2 reports nargs 0. The candidate declares char const* __cdecl(void). The adapted pointer return type is the recorded ABI adaptation; the argument contract (none) is identical.

checks.name: constants_and_scaling
checks.rationale: The only retail constant is the absolute global address 0x005C8BD4 encoded in the moffs load a1d48b5c00. There is no scaling, arithmetic or index computation. The candidate body contains no source constant; the load address is the linker relocation of the AppTitle symbol at .bss+0 in the fresh object.

checks.name: memory_layout_and_access
checks.rationale: Retail performs exactly one 4-byte read from 0x005C8BD4 and does not access 0x005C8BC0. The corrected candidate performs exactly one 4-byte read of the distinct 4-byte global AppTitle and never reads InstanceHandle; the fresh -O3 object encodes it as `mov <dir32 .bss+0>,%eax`. The previous candidate returned InstanceHandle (.bss+4), which the retail bytes cannot do because their moffs operand is 0x005C8BD4.

checks.name: calls_and_side_effects
checks.rationale: Retail has no call instructions and no side effects: it only reads 0x005C8BD4. The candidate calls nothing and writes nothing; the host differential re-read AppTitle, InstanceHandle and CommandLine after each call and found them unchanged.

checks.name: return_and_error_paths
checks.rationale: Retail has one basic block, one return and no error branch; EAX is the loaded dword. The candidate likewise has one return path returning the loaded global. In the ad-hoc differential all ten 32-bit values, including 0x00000000, 0x80000000 and 0xFFFFFFFF, were returned bit-for-bit by both the retail ESIL execution and the host-built candidate.

checks.name: floating_point_semantics
checks.rationale: The body performs no floating-point load, store or arithmetic and reads no FPU state.

limitations: The reviewed scope is the single getter path; the function has no alternate or error path.

CFG evidence is retail-image structure only: Binary Ninja and Radare2 independently recover the same one-block retail graph, and cfg_similarity 1.0 measures their agreement, not candidate-versus-retail similarity.

Candidate structural equivalence rests on the identical one-block load/return shape, the fresh -O3 object and the ten-case retail-ESIL/host differential, not on a paired runtime capture. A paired typed Frida capture of retail igi.exe and the staged candidate is outstanding.
The ten-case host differential is an ad-hoc command, not a committed case in scripts/native_diff_runner.py; no committed runner case exists for this address.

The candidate AppTitle global has no writer in the engine build because retail 0x0048F100 (SetAppTitle) is only an unlinked GameNatives transcription. Retail 0x005C8BD4 holds 0x0053B534 ("Innerloop") after start-up while the candidate AppTitle stays null, so end-to-end start-up behaviour still differs until that setter is reconstructed in-tree. This record claims the getter's structure and global identity only.
The semantic name GetAppTitle is inferred from the retail writer 0x0048F100 (SetWindowTextA with "Innerloop") and the reader's MessageBoxA caption use; it is a project name, not a retail symbol.
The retail-to-candidate global mapping is by symbol and 4-byte width; this review does not establish process-wide memory-layout equivalence.
